script: Spread and total were not saved for LAC at SEA, so this script is inferred only from Weeks 1-3 form. Seattle's defense has allowed 3.37 yards per carry, 5 runs of 10-plus, and 2 passes of 20-plus yards on 99 attempts, while the Chargers have allowed 4.00 yards per carry, 8 runs of 10-plus, and 9 explosives on 99 attempts with 9.47 YPA on 38 left-side throws. That form points to Seattle moving it through Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 36 targets and 405 yards plus an Emanuel Wilson/J.Price carry split (32 and 28), and to Omarion Hampton's 50 carries and 193 yards running into a 3.37-YPC front rather than a soft box.
who_goes_off: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should go off: 405 receiving yards on 36 targets over three games, 135 yards a game and 11.25 yards per target, into a Chargers defense that has allowed 9.47 YPA on the left (38 attempts), 7.93 YPA on the right (30 attempts), and 9 passes of 20-plus yards. Ladd McConkey is the Chargers' efficient answer at 183 yards on 15 targets and 208 air yards, but Seattle has allowed only 2 explosives on 99 attempts, so that 12.2 yards-per-target rate is the one most likely to get cut.
weak_spot: The Chargers' weak spot is the left side at 9.47 yards per attempt on 38 throws, with the right also soft at 7.93 on 30 attempts and the middle their best number at 5.67 on 24; no zone-or-man split was saved, so this is location, not a guessed nickel tell. Seattle has no matching hole — left 5.78 YPA on 40 attempts, middle 4.93 on 14, right 4.11 on 38 — and the run front is a strength at 3.37 yards per carry with only 5 runs of 10-plus.
injury_fallout: No injury list was saved for LAC at SEA, so the only fallout on the sheet is the usage already logged. Omarion Hampton has 50 carries for 193 yards to Keaton Mitchell's 17 for 85 and K.Vidal's 1 for 6, while Seattle is split among Emanuel Wilson (32 carries, 109 yards), J.Price (28 carries, 119 yards), and George Holani (15 carries, 52 yards), with D.Lock the only quarterback rush logged at 1 carry for 14 yards.
qb_vs_blitz: Justin Herbert is -0.46 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 25 dropbacks and -0.03 when not blitzed, and Seattle blitzes only 20%, so he mostly avoids the look that has wrecked him without becoming efficient in the clean look. Seattle's QB is +0.47 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 43 dropbacks and +0.15 with no blitz, and the Chargers blitz 25%, so that pressure rate has fueled Seattle's passing game and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 36 targets rather than slowing them.

picks.why: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 405 receiving yards on 36 targets in three games, 135 a game, against a 93.5 line, and the Chargers have allowed 9.47 YPA on 38 left-side attempts plus 9 passes of 20-plus yards on 99 attempts. They also blitz 25% into a Seattle QB at +0.47 EPA versus the blitz on 43 dropbacks, so the volume and the soft side of the field both sit on the over.

Quentin Johnston has 64 receiving yards on 17 targets and 171 air yards, 21.3 yards a game and 3.8 yards per target, well under a 34.5 line. Seattle has allowed 2 passes of 20-plus yards on 99 attempts and only 4.11 to 5.78 YPA by side, so the downfield profile that has not converted is the exact look this defense has taken away.
